attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use comments to create multiple sections in the editor to better organize your code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What code might be placed underneath each comment?

❓ How do you create blank lines in the JavaScript editor?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that typing // tells the project to skip over the text that follows and move onto the next line of code. Just as when naming sprites, it’s useful to be short and descriptive when writing comments. 

💡 Point out to the ninja that they are welcome to use different images or variable names in this project. They can click the palette to change the image.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by adding code comments to organize where the code will go in the editor!


Notice there is already code in the editor; there are three sprite images under the comment // sprite images that can be used in the project. 


Underneath this starter code, add comments with these descriptions to the project: array set up, game events.


Start each comment with // and add several blank lines between each comment.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you declare a new array and type the image variable names inside the brackets [ ]?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How was an array created in the blocks editor? How is it similar and different to creating an array in the JavaScript editor?

❓ What keywords and symbols do you notice in the array declaration code?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that an array is an ordered list of elements with the same data type. An array can be made up of image, string, number, or sprite values. All elements in the array must be of the same type.

💡 In the blocks editor, the ninja used a [set list to] block to create a new array. If the ninja wanted to create an array of a different type, they would drag in either an image or text bubble. Similarly, in the JavaScript editor, specific symbols need to be used to indicate the array type. For images, the ninja should use img `..`. In this example, the images are stored as variables, and the variable names can be typed directly into the array. 

💡 Arrays are declared the same way as variables in JavaScript. However, the elements of an array must be contained by brackets [ ]. Point out to the ninja that like other symbols such as parentheses or curly brackets, the matching bracket pair is automatically added in the JavaScript editor when the first pair is typed.
steps.instructions:
Use an array to store the 3 sprite images!


An array is an ordered list of elements with the same data type. Create an array in JavaScript that contains a list of image variables.


Underneath // array set up, use the keyword let to declare a new array called spriteList. Type an assignment operator, then use a pair of brackets [ ] to contain the elements in the array. 


Inside the brackets [ ], type the names of the 3 sprite image variables declared under // sprite images separated by commas, so that the code looks like:

let spriteList = [wizard, crystalBall, catStatue]

Now, the 3 sprite images are stored in the spriteList array to be used in the project.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use randint inside the brackets [ ] to select a random value, between 0 and the array length minus 1, from the spriteList array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should 1 be subtracted from the length of the spriteList array in the randint function’s maximum argument?

❓ What will happen when the A button is pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that the elements in an array are assigned an index, based on the order in which they are added. The index begins at 0, then increases by 1 for each element. 

💡 In this example, the randint function randomly selects a value between 0 and the length of the spriteList array minus 1. There are 3 elements in the array, so the length of the spriteList is 3. However, because the index of elements in the array begin at 0, the third element’s index is 2, not 3. As a result, 1 needs to be subtracted from the length of the spriteList array, so that the randint function randomly selects an element with an index between 0-2 as the sprite variable’s value.
steps.instructions:
Select a random sprite from the spriteList array. 


Open Controller and drag [run code on (button) button (event)] underneath // game events. Use the default property A and default event Pressed.


Use the keyword let and an assignment operator to declare a new variable called sprite. After the assignment operator, type the name of the array created in the previous step followed by a pair of brackets: spriteList[]


Inside the brackets [ ], use randint to select a random value from the array. Keep the minimum argument set to 0. For the maximum argument, type the name of the array followed by a dot operator to select the length property from the code completion tool. The length property returns the total number of elements in an array. 


Because arrays order elements beginning at 0, but the length property starts counting at 1, subtract 1 from spriteList.length, so that the variable randomly selects a value from the spriteList array with an index between 0-2.


Now, a random sprite image from the spriteList array will be stored in the sprite variable.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type 5 possible string responses, separated by commas, in the answerList array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What type of values should be added to the answerList array? What symbols need to surround each element to indicate their type?

❓ What responses might the sprite share with the user?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that an array is an ordered list of elements with the same data type. An array can be made up of images, string, number, or sprite values. All elements in the array must be of the same type.

💡 In the blocks editor, the ninja used a [set list to] block to create a new array. If the ninja wanted to create an array of a different type, they would drag in either an image or text bubble. Similarly, in the JavaScript editor, specific symbols need to be used to indicate the array type. For strings, quotation marks should be placed around each element.
steps.instructions:
Add another array to store random answers for the sprite to share with the user!


Underneath // array set up, use the keyword let to declare another array called answerList. Type an assignment operator, then use a pair of brackets [ ] to contain the elements in the array. 


The answerList array will contain a list of string values. Inside the brackets [ ], type 5 possible responses to questions that the user might ask in quotation marks, separated by commas. The code might look like: 


let answerList = [“I think yes”, “Ask again later”] 

Inside the controller.A event underneath // game events, declare a new variable called answer. Assign the variable a random value from the answerList array by typing answerList and a pair of brackets [ ] to the right of the assignment operator.


Inside the brackets [ ], use randint to select a random value from the array between 0 and the length of the answerList array minus 1.


Now, a random string value from the answerList array will be stored in the answer variable.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set the range of the randint function to select a number from 0 to numberList.length - 1?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What type of values should be added to the numberList array? What symbols need to surround each element to indicate their type? 

❓ What do you notice about the colors of each element in the 3 different arrays?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In the blocks editor, the ninja used a [set list to] block to create a new array. If the ninja wanted to create an array of a different type, they would drag in either an image or text bubble. Similarly, in the JavaScript editor, specific symbols need to be used to indicate the array type. For numbers, values can be directly entered into the array’s brackets, but must be separated by commas.

💡Point out to the ninja the different colors of the elements in each array: variables or images are black, strings are red, and numbers are green. These colors help the program and the coder identify the type of values found in each array.
steps.instructions:
Add a third array to store number values to set a random background color!


Underneath // array set up, use the keyword let to declare a third array called numberList. Type an assignment operator, then use a pair of brackets [ ] to contain the elements in the array. 


The numberList array will contain a list of number values. Inside the brackets [ ], type 5 different numbers between 0 and 15, separated by commas. The code might look like:

let numberList = [2, 4, 5, 6, 10]

Then, declare a new variable called color inside the controller.A event underneath // game events. Assign the variable a random value from the numberList array by typing numberList and a pair of brackets [ ] to the right of the assignment operator. 


Inside the brackets [ ], use randint and numberList.length to select a random value from the numberList array, using the same formatting from the sprite and answer variables.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you create a sprite inside the controller.A event that will use the stored sprite image from the spriteList array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when the A button is pressed?

❓ How are the 3 variables and array values used in the setBackgroundColor and sprites.create code?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja how each variable pulls a random value from each array, then uses it in the code below. The sprite variable pulls a random sprite image from the spriteList array, which is then used as the image parameter in the sprites.create code. The color variable pulls a random number from the numberList array, which is then used as the color parameter in the setBackgroundColor code.

💡 When the A button is pressed, the stored background color and sprite image will appear in the center of the screen.
steps.instructions:
Use the variables to add the stored background color and sprite image to the project!


Open Scene and drag [set background color to (color)] underneath the 3 variable declarations inside the controller.A event. Inside the parentheses, replace 0 with the color variable, so that the background color is set to a random value from the numberList array.


Open Sprites and drag [sprite (img) of kind (kind)] underneath the background color code. Update the sprite name to answerSprite, then replace the image parameter with the sprite variable, so that the Player sprite uses a random sprite image value from the spriteList array.


Set the Player sprite’s position by opening Sprites and dragging [set (mySprite) position to x y] underneath the Player sprite creation code. Update the x and y parameters so that the Player sprite appears in the center of the screen. 


Click ▶ to see a random background color and a random sprite image appear on screen every time the A button is pressed!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add the setScale function inside the controller.A event, and update the value and anchor parameters so that the Player sprite resizes from its center?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What does the setScale function do? How might you use it in a project?

❓ How would you change the value and anchor parameters to make the sprite resize in different ways?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that the setScale function assigns the sprite a scale based on the image’s dimension. To increase the size of a sprite’s image, the ninja should use a value greater than 1 as the value parameter. To decrease the size of a sprite’s image, the ninja should use a value between 0-1 as the value parameter. To change the location of the image that is pinned in place, the ninja can delete .Middle, retype the dot operator, then select a different position from the code completion tool for the anchor parameter.
steps.instructions:
Change the size of the Player sprite on the screen!


Set the Player sprite’s scale by opening Sprites and dragging [set (mySprite) scale to (1) anchor (ScaleAnchor.Middle)] underneath the Player sprite’s position code. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text: 

mySprite.setScale(1, ScaleAnchor.Middle)

The setScale function takes 2 parameters: value and anchor. The value parameter sets the value that the image’s dimensions will be multiplied by, and the anchor parameter sets the location of the image that is pinned in place while the rest of the image is resized.


Replace mySprite with the Player sprite’s name. Change the value parameter from 1 to 3, so that the Player sprite’s width and height are multiplied by 3. Use the default anchor property ScaleAnchor.Middle, so that the Player sprite grows from its center. 


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite appear 3x larger on the screen!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add a pause after each sayText so that there is time for the Player sprite to think and respond?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens when the A button is pressed? How is the answer variable used in the sayText code?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja how the answer variable pulls a random string from the answerList array, which is then used as the text parameter in the sayText code.
steps.instructions:
Code the Player sprite to respond to a user’s question! 


Open Sprites and drag [(this) say (:))] underneath the Player sprite’s position code, inside the controller.A event. Update the string parameter so the Player sprite shows that it’s thinking about the answer, then set how long the text will stay on screen by updating the duration parameter.


Add a pause below the sayText code, set to the same value as the duration parameter. Then, open Music and drag [play (toPlay) (playbackMode)] underneath pause. Use the dot operator to select a sound to play when the Player sprite is ready to answer!


Open Sprites and add another[(this) say (:))] underneath the play code. This time, set the string parameter to the answer variable, so that the Player sprite shares the random string stored from the answerList array. Update the duration parameter and add another pause, set to the same value. 


Click ▶ to ask the Player sprite a question, then press the A button to see what its response is!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use destroy to remove the sprite so the user can press the A button to see another sprite appear?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should the sprite disappear at the end of the controller.A code?

❓ Did you match the pause parameter to the same value as the duration parameter in the sayText code?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that each time the user presses the A button, the project should reset and the sprite should disappear. Without the destroy code, another sprite would be placed on top of the existing code when the A button is pressed again.
steps.instructions:
Encourage the user to ask another question! 


Open Sprites and drag [(this) say (:))] underneath the last pause, inside the controller.A event. Update the string and duration parameters, so that the Player sprite encourages the user to ask another question then press the A button. Add another pause set to the same value as the duration parameter, below the sayText code.


Open Sprites and drag [destroy (mySprite)] underneath pause. Replace mySprite with the Player sprite’s name, then add an effect parameter, too. 


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite tell the user to ask another question, then disappear from the screen.

steps.hints: ❓ What directions would help players understand how the game is played?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What directions might tell the user how to play the game? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that strings need to be placed inside of quotation marks and that parameters need to be separated by a comma, otherwise the code will not be able to run correctly.
steps.instructions:
Finish the project by adding directions for the user!


Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] on a blank line above the controller.A event, underneath the // game events. Update the string and layout parameters, so that the dialog box tells the user to ask the Player sprite a question.


Click ▶ to see the completed project!

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses arrays to randomize how a sprite responds to a user’s question!

validationItems.text: Create a spriteList array to contain 3 sprite image variables.
Create an answerList array to contain 5 string responses.
Create a colorList array to contain 5 numbers between 0 and 15.
When the A button is pressed, select a random sprite image, answer, and number.
Create a sprite and change the background image based on the three randomly selected values.
Use setScale to change the size of the player sprite.
Use pause and sayText functions to make the player sprite respond to the user.
Destroy the player sprite after they have revealed the answer to the user.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and several functions available to help you create and update arrays in JavaScript. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Making a List, Checking it Twice
badges.description: Create and modify arrays within a program in JavaScript.

badges.title: Array of Sunshine
badges.description: Create an array in JavaScript.

badges.title: A Lengthy Calculation
badges.description: Calculate the length of an array.

badges.title: I Choose You!
badges.description: Access an element based on its index in an array.

badges.title: Objects May Be Larger Than They Appear
badges.description: Change the scale of a sprite.

badges.title: You’ll Fit Right In
badges.description: Use the push function to add an element to the end of an array.

badges.title: A String of Questions
badges.description: Use the askForString function to prompt the user for a string response.

badges.title: For Each Its Own
badges.description: Use a for element of loop to iterate through all the elements in an array.

badges.title: Search Engine
badges.description: Use the indexOf function to find the index of a provided value in an array.

badges.title: You’re Outta Here
badges.description: Use the removeAt function to remove a specific element from an array.
